description: A quiet question about where Gorgon sleeps changes how Alden sees the people watching him.

planning.storytellingVoice: Intimate character drama: two lonely people; concern that accidentally touches a painful subject.
planning.desire: Understand how Gorgon lives and keep him company.
planning.obstacle: Gorgon deflects concern and cannot leave; Alden cannot read his alien emotional cues.
planning.earlyCare: The person everyone passes has no room of his own.
planning.payoff: Alden recognizes why the photographs are cruel, rather than merely foolish.
planning.continuingQuestion: How can Alden show care without turning Gorgon into an object of pity?
planning.direction: Hold the conversation in shared framing; show Alden receiving the dismissal and the celebrity remark; final shared still lets the confinement land. Pixel performances follow each passage only after three encounters.

signatures.Alden: Tired rambling practical questions, then hesitant attention; thoughtful face and chin-rest.
signatures.Gorgon: Brief factual replies and deflection; restrained attentive expressions, no human-style crying.

opening.style: Hand-cut woodblock print in indigo, cream and muted moss
opening.moment: Alden rests on the desk and acknowledges the pain of being alone.
opening.speaker: Alden
opening.dialogue: 一个人的时候，有时候真的不好受。

continuation.end: Alden learns Gorgon has no room, asks about food and loneliness, and realizes that unwanted attention is cruel because Gorgon cannot escape cameras. He has not yet proposed crickets.
continuation.nextEndBefore: “I understand. But you really reached all the way
continuation.note: Alden reins in pity, proposes live crickets and checks that unusual offerings will not offend. Gorgon appreciates them but calls his disclosure a costly moment of melancholy. Stop before Alden challenges acquaintanceship versus friendship.
